exposure: Conventional postnatal screening for familial retinoblastoma
Prenatal RB1 mutation identification followed by planned early-term delivery
outcome: Age at first tumor in each eye
Treatment success (avoidance of enucleation or external-beam irradiation)
cohort: The study included twenty children with familial retinoblastoma born between 1996 and 2014, divided into two groups: those undergoing conventional postnatal screening and those identified by prenatal RB1 mutation for planned early-term delivery.
finding: Prenatal molecular diagnosis with planned early-term delivery for infants with familial retinoblastoma significantly improved outcomes, leading to fewer detectable tumors at birth, better vision, and less invasive therapy compared to conventional postnatal screening.
mod_finding: Planned early-term delivery (36-38 weeks' gestation) was a key component of the successful prenatal diagnosis strategy and was not associated with any reported complications.
gest_age: 36-38 weeks' gestation (for planned early-term delivery cohort)
